brief: GS tracks Nasdaq futures positioning through an Oct 13-20 selloff and a Meta-driven shock. Despite the index losing 3.5% over Oct 13-20, Non-Dealer net positioning (per CFTC) reached a new nominal high: Non-Dealers bought $9.5bn, a third straight week of buying for a cumulative $21.8bn since Sept 29. Meta's earnings disappointment then triggered short reinstatements: on Oct 22 Meta fell 7.0%, leading a broad AI-related decline (HyperScalers -4.1%, Memory -8.6%, Semiconductors -6.5%), Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and futures open interest jumped $10.6bn, the largest one-day rise of 2026 excluding roll periods, as funding underperformed and sizeable shorts were initiated. From Oct 22-26 markets stabilized: Nasdaq recouped 1.1%, open interest retraced $9bn, as tactical shorts covered and longs also cut as funding cheapened, likely CTA-driven given a momentum-framework break. Net: length remains elevated heading into Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet earnings; a disappointment there could trigger meaningful futures selling.
